**Maybe—but I’d be cautious about calling Wiggle & Snug Snug-Fit Overnight Diapers “better” unless you can verify their absorbency and fit for your child.** I couldn’t find strong independent testing for that exact product, so I’d treat them as a **trial option**, not a proven upgrade.

For nighttime leaks, the most important things are:

- **More absorbency than daytime diapers.** Overnight diapers are typically designed for longer wear and often have substantially more capacity than regular diapers. Babylist notes many overnight diapers offer about **25–50% more capacity**, and are intended for around **12 hours** of protection. ([babylist.com](https://www.babylist.com/hello-baby/best-overnight-diapers))  
- **Snug but not tight fit.** A snug waist/thigh fit helps prevent gaps, but if the diaper is too tight—or compressed by tight pajamas—it can actually make leaks worse. Pampers recommends no gaps at the waist/thighs and checking that leg cuffs aren’t tucked in; Albee Baby also notes that too-tight diapering can reduce absorbency. ([support.pampers.com](https://support.pampers.com/hc/en-us/articles/21678052813597-How-can-I-prevent-diaper-leakage-and-protect-my-baby-s-skin)) ([albeebaby.com](https://www.albeebaby.com/blogs/from-the-cradle/overnight-diaper-leaks))  
- **The leak pattern.** Front leaks may need a forward booster pad or penis pointed down; leg leaks often mean fit/ruffles/tabs; back leaks may need a higher-rise diaper or center/back booster. ([albeebaby.com](https://www.albeebaby.com/blogs/from-the-cradle/overnight-diaper-leaks))  

**My practical take:** If Wiggle & Snug is marketed as an overnight diaper and fits your child well, it’s worth trying a small pack—especially if your current diaper is soaked by morning. But if leaks continue, I’d compare it against well-tested overnight options like **Pampers Swaddlers Overnights**, **Huggies OverNites**, or an **overnight diaper + booster pad** setup. BabyGearLab’s testing, for example, rated Pampers Swaddlers Overnights highly for overnight absorbency, while noting Huggies OverNites had strong leak scores but more mixed lab results. ([babygearlab.com](https://www.babygearlab.com/topics/diapering-potty/best-overnight-diaper))

**Best first experiment:** use one size up in an overnight diaper, make sure the leg ruffles are fully out, avoid tight pajamas, and add a booster pad if the diaper is totally saturated by morning.
